Entry requirements · 2027 entry

Economics BS at MIT

What MIT asks of applicants to Economics BS for 2027 entry (the 2026–27 application cycle). Each requirement below is labelled verified, partly verified or not verified, with the date it was checked and a link to the official source.

US · All MIT courses · Economics & Finance field guide

Entry requirements 2027 entry 7 of 8 verified
SAT / ACT
  • SAT or ACT required — prospective first-year and transfer students
  • ACT writing/science sections and the SAT optional essay are not required
  • Required tests must be taken before November 30 (Early Action) or December 31 (Regular Action)

MIT states no cutoff or recommended SAT/ACT scores. MIT admits to the Institute, not to a major: these admissions pages apply to all first-year applicants, whatever the intended major.

Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — International applicants · MIT: First-year applicants — Deadlines & requirements
English language
  • English proficiency exam strongly recommended (not stated as required) for non-native English speakers who have used English for fewer than five years or do not speak English at home or in school
  • Accepted: TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test, Cambridge English (C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency)
  • MIT minimum / recommended scores:
    • TOEFL 90 / 100 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 5 / 5.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026)
    • IELTS 7 / 7.5
    • PTE Academic 65 / 70
    • Cambridge 185 / 190
    • Duolingo 120 / 125

These are minimum and recommended scores MIT publishes for its English tests, not admitted-student figures. Regular Action applicants must take any English proficiency test before January 31.

Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — Tests & scores
Admissions tests

None listed on the official source

No course-specific admissions test; the only required tests are the SAT or ACT, for all first-year applicants.

Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — Deadlines & requirements
Subject prerequisites
  • Not used in Altiora’s matching yet — see the note for the official guidance

Official: MIT has no required high school classes. For students in an American curriculum it looks at math including calculus; science, including physics, chemistry and/or biology; and some challenging humanities, arts and social sciences courses, and recommends at least introductory coursework in physics, chemistry and biology if available. These are recommendations for all applicants, not major-specific.

Partly verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — International applicants · MIT: Preparing for MIT — Academic foundations
A-Level requirements
Grades
Not recorded
Details
The school transcript should include results of external examinations such as A Levels that are required for university entrance in the home country; MIT asks for predicted grades if available. A Levels scores are self-reported in the application’s Test scores section (official scores are not required at application).

MIT does not convert grades to the American system and states no A-Level grade or IB points requirement. Only admitted students are required to send final grades.

Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — International applicants · MIT: First-year applicants — Tests & scores
IB requirements
Overall score
Not recorded
Details
The school transcript should include results of external examinations such as the International Baccalaureate that are required for university entrance in the home country; MIT asks for predicted grades if available. the International Baccalaureate scores are self-reported in the application’s Test scores section (official scores are not required at application).

MIT does not convert grades to the American system and states no A-Level grade or IB points requirement. Only admitted students are required to send final grades.

Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — International applicants · MIT: First-year applicants — Tests & scores
Other qualifications
  • Advanced Placement and other exam scores (e.g. IB, A-level, Baccalauréat): self-reported in the Test scores section of the application
  • Official score reports are not required at application; scores are verified upon enrollment
Verified19 Oct 2026MIT: First-year applicants — Tests & scores
Other requirements
  • Interview:
    • offered by an MIT Educational Counselor when one is available
    • if none is available it is waived without disadvantage
  • Creative portfolios (research, music & theater arts, visual art & architecture, maker): optional
  • Two teacher letters of recommendation required (one math/science and one humanities/social science/language recommended)
